Volume 10 · Chapter 12

Quantitative model governance

Graduate Author-reviewed · Prerequisites: v10-c11

By the endValidate pricing and risk models against independent benchmarks and failure scenarios.

Decide what a model may be used for, and why

Capability. Design and defend an evidence-based decision about a quantitative model's permitted use. You will separate mathematical specification, implementation, calibration, empirical performance and operational control; quantify several sources of uncertainty; and write an actionable validation finding. The immediate prerequisite is incomplete markets and advanced derivatives. We use dated discounting, replication, Greeks and numerical error from this volume, the linear algebra of systems and identification, and the statistical interpretation of estimation and inference.

Sable's valuation team has a program that reproduces two calibration quotes exactly. Its sponsor wants permission to price a much larger book, extend the maturity range and release the result today. A spreadsheet of passing test counts accompanies the request. What has actually been established? A correct program can implement the wrong contract. A well-fitted model can leave an important parameter unidentified. Small errors per instrument can become material on a large position. A reviewer must connect the evidence to the decision, rather than translate “many checks passed” into unconditional permission.

Every Sable price, position, comparison outcome, identity and decision threshold in this chapter is original synthetic teaching material. Currency amounts are CU unless stated otherwise. The lab evaluates a declared fictional policy; it does not approve any actual model or interpret a real institution's legal duties. Its deterministic workflow rules are controls around quantitative evidence, not themselves a claim to belong to a regulator's particular definition of a model.

1. Give each claim its own evidence

Start with the intended decision and cash contract. “Price an option” is incomplete: identify exercise and settlement dates, payoff units, dividends, credit and collateral rights, permitted trades, funding, input timestamps, and the quantity exposed to the result. Then write the mathematical target. An expectation under a chosen Q is a model value; an estimate of physical loss under P is a different object. The difference is economic, not a choice of variable name.

Verification asks whether the implementation computes its specified mathematical target within a stated numerical tolerance. Exact small cases, independent formulas, limiting cases, algebraic invariants, dimensional checks and a genuinely different implementation can supply evidence. Comparing two wrappers around the same faulty library is weak independence. A zero PDE residual computed with the same incorrect derivatives as the price can also be a shared-error check.

Calibration selects parameters using designated observations and an objective. Record which quotes enter, their rights and timestamps, the weights, constraints, optimizer, stopping tolerance and competing solutions. A small objective establishes only that the selected model reproduces those inputs according to that metric. It does not establish unique parameters, stable extrapolation, a physical law, or forecast accuracy on the observations used to fit it.

Validation evaluates whether the specification, inputs, computations and observed behavior are adequate for the intended use, and identifies the limitations that remain. A validator may agree that code is correct while rejecting a use outside its supported domain. Conversely, a numerical discrepancy should first be traced through conventions, units and data before it is interpreted as evidence against an economic mechanism. A price difference from a dealer quote is not automatically model error: the quote may incorporate different terms, spreads, inventory or stale information.

Monitoring asks whether the evidence supporting an existing permission still applies. Data can become stale, exposures can increase, products can change, or a newly observed failure can matter even though no source-code line changed. Governance assigns an accountable owner, a reviewer capable of challenging the work, a person or body with decision authority, and an escalation path. A recorded limit without a means to detect and respond to its breach does little work.

As dated US context, the Federal Reserve's 17 April 2026 SR 26-2 letter supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8. The interagency attachment describes a tailored approach, expected to be most relevant above $30 billion in assets, with qualifications for smaller institutions. It is guidance rather than enforceable prescriptive standards. Its definition excludes simple arithmetic and certain rule-based software, and its footnote excludes generative and agentic AI. Those boundaries do not imply that excluded tools need no controls. Our cases concern quantitative financial models and use explicitly invented decision rules; the agency document does not prescribe Sable's thresholds or certify this curriculum.

2. Reconcile a discrepancy before assigning a cause

Let V be the specified mathematical model value and V̂ its computed approximation. Let P* denote a separately defined comparison target for the actual decision. Algebra gives V̂ − P* = (V̂ − V) + (V − P*). The first component is computational error relative to the mathematical model; the second combines specification and target mismatch. If input x is measured with error, insert V(x) and V(x̂) as additional intermediate terms. This is an accounting decomposition, not a statistical identification result. When V and P* are unknown, the labels alone do not estimate the terms.

Use a tolerance with units and purpose. An absolute tolerance of 10−6 CU per claim differs from a relative tolerance, a yield tolerance, a probability tolerance or a portfolio-loss limit. Relative error is unsuitable as the only criterion for an option whose exact price is zero or extremely small. A numerical method may meet an absolute price tolerance while a difference quotient for gamma remains inaccurate: differencing can amplify its errors. Each output needs a criterion matched to its use.

When possible, preserve a small independently reproducible counterexample. Record the exact contract, data version, parameter domain, executable invocation, expected result, actual result and financial consequence. A finding such as “stale terminal discount produces a 21 CU overvaluation per bond and 840 CU on the requested holding” gives a decision maker more information than “test 27 failed.” The repair should address the cause and rerun affected comparisons; increasing the tolerance to hide the difference changes the acceptance criterion.

Worked example 1 — Correct arithmetic can use the wrong input

A synthetic bond pays 100, 100 and 2100 CU at years 1, 2 and 3. The benchmark discount vector for the agreed valuation timestamp is (0.98,0.94,0.88). Its value is 100(0.98)+100(0.94)+2100(0.88)=2040 CU. A candidate uses 0.89 for the last discount and otherwise identical inputs. It returns 2061 CU. The 21 CU difference is entirely 2100(0.01); the other two cash contributions agree.

The candidate's summation can be arithmetically perfect. The comparison has exposed an input-version mismatch, assuming the benchmark timestamp and curve are indeed the intended target. For a long holding of 40 bonds the marked difference is 840 CU. A short holding would reverse that signed exposure. An absolute acceptance tolerance of 0.000001 CU per bond is plainly breached. The appropriate response is to reconcile and bind the input version, then rerun valuation and affected downstream reports; this case alone does not justify changing the economic discounting model.

3. Exact calibration can leave the requested value unidentified

A parameter vector is identified by calibration data only if distinct permitted parameters cannot produce the same relevant observations. For a linear calibration y = Aθ, every vector z in the null space of A satisfies A(θ+z)=Aθ. Thus a unique fit does not follow from a small residual. A new linear target ℓ′θ is identified within that affine solution set exactly when ℓ′z=0 for every permitted null direction z. If this fails, varying a null direction changes the target without changing the fit.

Proof. Differences between any two exact solutions lie in ker A. If ℓ annihilates all those differences, the target is the same for every solution. If an allowed difference z has ℓ′z≠0, the two solutions give different targets. For the unrestricted affine set, the equivalent row-space condition ℓ∈row(A) follows from row(A) = ker(A)⊥, proved by orthogonality and rank–nullity. Parameter restrictions can remove some differences; state those restrictions rather than silently treating them as information supplied by the quotes.

Worked example 2 — Two matching bond quotes, many third-year values

Let P(t) be the price now of 100 CU paid at time t, evaluated only at the stated tenors. Consider the family P(t)=100+at+bt²+ct(t−1)(t−2). We know P(1)=98 and P(2)=94. The equations a+b=−2 and 2 a+4 b=−6 give a=−1, b=−1. The c term vanishes at both calibration tenors and at t=0. Every c fits those observations exactly.

At year 3, P(3)=88+6 c. An explicitly imposed scenario restriction −1≤c≤1 gives a range [82,94], width 12 CU per 100 CU payment. It is an assumption-conditioned sensitivity range, not a confidence interval. The two observed quotes did not estimate c or justify that restriction. All displayed payment-date prices are positive; we have imposed no nonnegative-forward-rate rule. A complete curve between other dates would require its own consistency and admissibility checks.

If Sable permits no more than a 2 CU range for the requested use, the three-year request fails that invented scope criterion. Restricting the use to year 2 gives the common value 94 and zero range. Obtaining reliable three-year information or justifying a tighter family is another possible remediation, but setting c=0 because it is the software default does not turn 88 into a data-identified answer.

This issue appears beyond curves. An incomplete market can fit traded claims while leaving an untraded payoff's price undetermined. Several volatility models can fit a selected option surface while implying different path-dependent exposures. A reported optimizer covariance matrix cannot repair structural nonidentification if its calculation has quietly fixed a free parameter. A reviewer should ask which values are identified, which depend on regularization or prior restrictions, and how the intended decision changes across those alternatives.

4. Identification and numerical stability are different tests

Even a unique solution can be highly sensitive to small data changes. Fit an affine price f(t)=α+βt through quotes y1,y2 at distinct t1,t2. At a target t, set w=(t−t1)/(t2−t1). Then f(t)=(1−w)y1+wy2. If the absolute error of each quote is at most ε,

|δf(t)| ≤ (|1−w|+|w|)ε.

This bound follows from the triangle inequality and is attainable when the two errors take the signs of their coefficients. Inside the interpolation interval, 0≤w≤1 and the factor is one. Outside it, the coefficients have opposite signs and the factor can be large. This is absolute conditioning for this specific input norm and output; it is not the same as relative matrix conditioning or a guarantee about actual quote accuracy. At coincident maturities the slope is not identified, and the formula must not divide by zero.

Worked example 3 — A one-cent perturbation moves a distant value by two CU

Take t1=1, t2=1.01, y1=99 and y2=98.99. The fit is α=100, β=−1 and f(3)=97. The target weights are −199 and 200. Increasing only the second quote by 0.01 changes f(3) by 2 CU, giving 99. If each quote can independently differ by at most 0.01, the worst target error is 399(0.01)=3.99 CU, attained by lowering the first quote 0.01 and raising the second 0.01.

The narrow tenor gap gives exact algebraic identification but unstable extrapolation. Higher arithmetic precision can reduce rounding in the calculation; it cannot remove the amplification of uncertain input quotes. For 10,000 units of a claim whose quote is per unit, the one-quote scenario moves marked value by 20,000 CU. Whether that matters depends on position, decision and offsetting exposures, not solely on the fit's number of decimal places.

For nonlinear calibration, local derivatives or an inverse Jacobian provide analogous diagnostics only where the relevant differentiability and invertibility conditions hold. Near zero vega, for example, small option-price uncertainty can become large implied-volatility uncertainty. A local derivative is not a global error bound when the perturbation crosses a boundary or changes the optimizer's active constraints. Refit meaningful perturbed inputs and compare the actual decision as well as the local estimate.

5. Translate comparisons into the book's units and signs

Suppose instrument i has a signed quantity ni and a candidate-minus-benchmark error ei. The signed book discrepancy is E=Σniei. Its sign matters: a positive candidate error on a short position reduces candidate book value. The gross comparison amount G=Σ|niei| bounds |E| and reveals cancellation. Neither measure alone describes all economic risk; the signed total measures this book's actual comparison, while the gross amount asks how much offsetting error it contains.

If a justified error bound |ei|≤εi holds simultaneously for the relevant claims, then |E|≤Σ|ni|εi. This is a deterministic simultaneous bound. If each ε is merely a pointwise sample standard error, inserting it into that formula does not create the stated simultaneous guarantee. Likewise, adding error variances requires covariance assumptions; common data, code and calibration choices can make errors move together.

Worked example 4 — Every unit check passes, but the requested book fails

Benchmark prices are (100,80,50), candidate prices (100.01,79.98,49.99), and signed quantities (200,−150,100). Unit errors are (0.01,−0.02,−0.01), each within an inclusive 0.02 tolerance. Position contributions are (2,3,−1) CU, giving signed discrepancy 4 CU and gross discrepancy 6 CU. The root-mean-square unit error is √0.0002≈0.014142136 CU.

Sable separately requires |E|≤3 and G≤5 for this use. Both book gates fail even though all three unit gates pass. The unit tolerances alone allow a conservative book bound (200+150+100)(0.02)=9 CU. Changing the middle holding to +150 changes the signed discrepancy to −2, which passes its 3 CU gate, while gross discrepancy remains 6 and still fails its own gate. Those are explicit policy choices, not universal statistical thresholds. They force the decision to acknowledge scale and cancellation.

A useful finding names which computation or assumption creates the material exposure, whether its direction is known, which positions depend on it, and which decisions may be affected. Do not report “risk reduced by diversification” merely because two error bars were added in quadrature. For example, two 1,000,000 CU terminal claims sharing a discount-factor error of 0.0005 each have 500 CU errors with the same cause. Their combined error is 1000 CU in that scenario. The value √(500²+500²)≈707.11 would require a different probabilistic interpretation and zero covariance; neither follows from the two numbers.

6. Use outcome evidence without redefining success after seeing it

Before observing evaluation outcomes, freeze the target, forecast rule, calibration window, contract matching, error metric and intended comparison. Separate data used for fitting, selecting the model and assessing the selected procedure. Disjoint record identifiers can detect direct overlap; they do not prove independence when two records share the same event, issuer, information release or later-revised input. Time order matters when the intended task is forecasting. A random split that leaks future data may answer a different question.

Let ej be forecast minus subsequent comparison value. Report its mean for signed bias and mean square for combined dispersion and bias, with units. For a realized sample, n−1Σe² = n−1Σ(e−ē)²+ē². This identity does not assume independence. Under additional IID finite-variance assumptions, sample variance divided by n estimates the variance of the sample mean. Dependence, selection, changing regimes and a reused holdout can invalidate that interpretation. The names “test set” and “standard error” do not establish the assumptions.

Sable's eight frozen synthetic errors are (−1,−1,0,0,1,1,2,2) CU. Their mean is 1/2, MSE 3/2, sample variance 10/7, and RMSE √(3/2)≈1.224744871 CU. If an IID model were additionally justified, the estimated standard error of the mean would be √(5/28)≈0.422577127 CU. The supplied invented list establishes no sampling law, so the lab labels that last quantity conditional on the assumption. It does not attach an asserted coverage probability or claim a reliable distributional conclusion from eight numbers.

A discrepancy can be informative even when a small sample does not identify its exact frequency. Reconcile known cash failures immediately; investigate clustered errors; distinguish lack of evidence for a problem from evidence of adequate performance. A model-use decision combines the consequence of being wrong with the strength and relevance of the evidence. It should state what new observation, exposure change or failure would trigger reevaluation.

7. Make permission specific and reversible

A review packet should bind an identifiable model specification, source/build version, parameter and input versions, intended instruments and dates, test evidence and known limitations. A digest identifies bytes; it does not prove that those bytes are economically correct. A human-readable release identifier is useful only if it resolves to an immutable artifact in the actual operating process. In the teaching lab, simple version labels illustrate the comparison rule; a real deployment would need the artifact-binding mechanism.

Write findings as claims that can be acted on. Include the observed failure, a reproducible example, affected use and consequence, severity with a reason, responsible owner, required repair or temporary restriction, evidence needed to close it, and a review date. “Investigate model risk” has no completion test. “Replace the stale year-3 curve, regenerate the 40-bond report, and have a reviewer independently reconcile the 840 CU change” does.

Assign authority separately from technical authorship. The developer explains design choices and repairs defects. A challenger independently assesses the evidence and can obtain a response. A decision owner accepts, restricts or refuses the requested use within the institution's authority structure. Identity differences alone do not prove independence or competence; access to evidence, incentives, expertise and power to escalate also matter. Audit of the process asks whether these controls operate; repeating every pricing calculation is a different task.

An exception must describe exactly what is relaxed, by whom, until when and subject to which compensating controls. It must also say what remains a blocking defect. A temporary size increase is not permission to use an unreviewed version or ignore a known valuation discrepancy. At expiry, the ordinary limit can resume even if the code has not changed. A limit on a measure that the process does not monitor cannot reliably constrain use.

Worked example 5 — A size exception does not erase a failed model gate

As of 6 October 2026, Sable requests 100,000 CU notional. The ordinary limit is 50,000. A separate fictional committee has recorded a size-only exception up to 120,000, inclusive through 13 October. The requested and reviewed version labels agree, developer and challenger differ, and evidence is two days old against a five-day threshold.

The size and administrative checks pass. Nevertheless the 21 CU bond discrepancy, 12 CU curve-family range and 4/6 CU signed/gross book discrepancies from the preceding cases fail their substantive gates. The lab returns reject_requested_use with those four named failures. It does not take the number of successful checks as a vote that outweighs the failed ones.

In a repaired scenario, use the benchmark bond discounts, restrict the curve request to the calibrated year 2, and reconcile the three candidate book prices to their benchmarks. All numerical/scope gates then pass; the same current size exception makes the request eligible_with_stated_limits under this fictional procedure. Expire the exception while keeping the 100,000 request: only the notional gate now fails. Reduce the request to 50,000: the ordinary limit suffices. Changing only the requested version still fails version binding even when all numerical comparisons happen to pass.

The recommendation is deliberately narrower than “the model is correct.” It means only that the named evidence passes the named case rules at the given date. It cannot establish an untested distribution, eliminate an unidentified parameter, authorize another institution's trading, or guarantee that a reviewer has exercised competent judgment. A defensible record keeps the permission and its uncertainty visible together.

Reproducible Sable review lab

Download the synthetic evidence inputs, standard-library Python model, complete reference output, standalone contract and instructions, and integrity manifest. The program independently exposes the bond cash differences, uncalibrated curve direction, affine conditioning weights, signed/gross book comparisons, descriptive holdout moments and the explicit policy gates. Financial arithmetic is rational except the labeled square-root approximations.

Try one intervention at a time. Change the candidate terminal discount; move the requested curve tenor to a calibrated date; widen the quote gap; reverse a position; make training/evaluation identifiers overlap; change the requested version; and expire the size exception. Predict the affected outputs first. Invalid shapes and undeclared numeric/date domains are rejected. A valid input can intentionally describe a failed review and return a rejection recommendation: a financially adverse scenario is not necessarily malformed data.

Exercises

  1. Trace a cash discrepancy. A new bond pays 50 and 1050 CU. Intended discounts are 0.99 and 0.95; a candidate uses 0.99 and 0.94. Find both values, candidate-minus-benchmark error and marked effect for a position of −20 bonds. Write a specific finding that distinguishes arithmetic from input-version agreement.
  2. Prove target identification. For y=Aθ and target ℓ′θ, prove the null-space criterion stated in Section 3. Apply it to Worked example 2. If c∈[−1/2,1/2] is imposed instead, give the three-year range and explain whether the original quotes supplied the tighter restriction.
  3. Conditioning transfer. Quotes 99 and 98.9 occur at tenors 1 and 1.1. Find the affine fit and value at year 3. With separate quote error bounds 0.01, find the worst target error and an attaining pair of perturbations. Compare with Worked example 3, then evaluate the conditioning factor at target 1.05.
  4. Prove and use a portfolio bound. Prove |Σniei|≤Σ|ni|εi when all |ei|≤εi. For quantities (100,−50,200) and bounds (0.01,0.03,0.005), calculate the bound and choose errors attaining it. Explain why individual one-standard-error estimates do not automatically provide this simultaneous guarantee.
  5. Audit the held-out errors. Derive the mean/MSE/variance decomposition and recompute Sable's eight-error metrics. An analyst subtracts the observed holdout mean from every forecast, then reports the reduced MSE on those same observations as independent evidence of improvement. Compute that reduced MSE and explain the evaluation problem and a feasible remedy.
  6. Common-source uncertainty. Recompute the combined discrepancy for two 1,000,000 CU claims with common discount error 0.0005. If instead each error is a centered random variable with standard deviation 500 CU, derive the standard deviation of their sum when correlation is 1, 0 and −1. State why the known common-shift scenario does not justify the correlation-zero calculation.
  7. A decision bound. A proposed trade has forecast gross advantage 12 CU. Its adverse model/input discrepancy is known, under a stated simultaneous scenario set, to be at most 5 CU, and execution/funding costs at most 4 CU. Prove a lower bound on net advantage. Repeat with forecast advantage 8. Does failure to obtain a positive lower bound prove that the trade loses money? Explain how the conclusion changes if “5” is only an estimated standard error.
  8. Run the policy counterfactual. Reproduce Worked example 5's baseline failed-gate list. Make precisely its three numerical/scope repairs, then separately (a) expire the exception one day before the as-of date, (b) reduce the requested notional to 50000 under that expired exception, and (c) change the requested version while restoring the original valid exception. Give the expected recommendation and relevant gate for each scenario.
  9. Write an exception that can be closed. A sponsor asks to ignore the curve's unidentified year-3 value until a future market-data release and to call the result “validated.” Draft a decision record with scope, quantitative consequence, owner, independent challenge, expiry, trigger and closure evidence. Explain which parts can legitimately be time-limited and which mathematical claim the current evidence cannot establish. Give explicit grading criteria for an acceptable alternative response.
  10. Referee the validation memo. A memo argues that exact calibration proves a unique correct model, many passed code tests guarantee empirical validity, per-instrument tolerance controls every portfolio, disjoint row IDs prove independent evaluation, and a size exception authorizes an unreviewed version. Correct every claim using at least two quantitative examples from this chapter. Propose a reproducible review packet and explain the limited role of the dated US guidance without presenting invented thresholds as agency requirements.
Complete solutions and evaluation criteria
  1. The intended value is 50(0.99)+1050(0.95)=49.5+997.5=1047 CU. The candidate is 49.5+987=1036.5 CU, so its error is−10.5 CU. Multiplying by the signed position−20 gives a +210 CU candidate-minus-benchmark book difference. A precise finding identifies the second discount's version/timestamp mismatch, the exact two-cash reproducer, affected−20 position and 210 CU marked consequence, assigned input owner, required curve reconciliation and independent rerun. The summation formula itself need not be wrong. If the candidate intentionally represents another valuation timestamp, first repair the comparison contract rather than accuse it of miscalculating its own target.
  2. For any exact solutions θ1,θ2, A(θ1−θ2)=0. A target annihilating every such feasible difference is constant across the solution set. Conversely a feasible difference z with ℓ′z≠0 gives two different target values at the same fitted data. For unrestricted exact solutions, these differences form ker A, with orthogonal complement row(A). In the polynomial example the coefficient direction (0,0,1) leaves both observations unchanged but moves the year-3 target by 6 per unit c. It is therefore unidentified. With imposed c∈[−1/2,1/2], the range is [85,91], width 6. The tighter restriction narrows the range but was not learned from the two quotes; its rationale and sensitivity must be documented separately.
  3. Slope is(98.9−99)/(1.1−1)=−1, intercept 100, and year-3 value97. Now w=(3−1)/0.1=20, so weights are−19,20. The bound is(19+20)(0.01)=0.39 CU, attained by quote perturbations(−0.01,+0.01), giving target 97.39. It is smaller than 3.99 because the calibration tenor gap is ten times wider, although this comparison is not a universal statement about unrelated curve models. At 1.05, w=1/2 and the factor is1, with maximum error 0.01. Coincident tenors would not identify the slope.
  4. The triangle inequality gives |Σniei|≤Σ|niei|=Σ|ni||ei|≤Σ|ni|εi. Here the bound is 100(0.01)+50(0.03)+200(0.005)=3.5 CU. Errors(0.01,−0.03,0.005) give contributions(1,1.5,1), attaining positive 3.5; reversing all signs attains−3.5. An estimated standard deviation is not an almost-sure bound. Even probabilistic marginal intervals need their joint coverage and dependence handled before they become a simultaneous statement; the deterministic proof cannot supply missing statistical assumptions.
  5. Write ej=(ej−ē)+ē, square and sum. The cross term vanishes because Σ(ej−ē)=0. Thus MSE=((n−1)/n)s²+ē². Here Σe=4 and Σe²=12, so ē=1/2, MSE=3/2, centered sum of squares 12−8(1/2)²=10, and unbiased-form sample variance10/7. RMSE is√(3/2); the IID-conditional standard error is√((10/7)/8)=√(5/28). Subtracting the sample mean makes the same-sample mean zero and MSE 10/8=5/4. This is a fitted intercept correction using the evaluation outcomes. It is not independent evidence that the selected correction will improve future performance. Treat those observations as development/selection data, freeze the adjusted rule and evaluate it on new appropriate outcomes, preserving time/information restrictions and reporting sample uncertainty under justified assumptions.
  6. The common deterministic scenario gives 500 CU on each claim and 1000 CU combined. For centered random errors with standard deviations 500, Var(E1+E2)=500²+500²+2ρ(500²). Standard deviations are1000 atρ=1, 500√2≈707.106781 atρ=0, and0 atρ=−1. The last case represents perfect offset of these centered random errors, not absence of all model uncertainty. The shared discount shift has the same direction and source in both positions; it is not a statement of independent centered draws. Replacing its 1000 scenario consequence by 707.11 silently changes the question.
  7. Let true gross advantage in the declared scenario set be 12+δ with δ≥−5, and cost k≤4. Net is 12+δ−k≥3 CU. With forecast 8 the bound is−1 CU, so the assumptions no longer certify a positive net result. They do not prove a loss: δ=0,k=4 gives net 4, while δ=−5,k=4 gives−1. If 5 is only an estimated standard error, it is not a deterministic lower-tail limit. A probabilistic decision then needs a distribution or concentration argument, parameter uncertainty and an explicit risk criterion; the preceding sure lower bound does not apply.
  8. The baseline failed gates arenumeric_benchmark, curve_scope, book_signed, book_gross. Individual book price tolerances pass; the size exception, version labels, challenger and evidence age also pass. Repair by setting candidate bond discounts to benchmark discounts, requested curve tenor to 2, and candidate book prices to benchmarks. The resulting request iseligible_with_stated_limits, under the fictional policy, with effective size limit 120000. (a) Set exception expiry 2026-10-05 against as-of 2026-10-06: effective limit 50000 andreject_requested_use, failed gatenotional_limit. (b) Also reduce request to 50000: equality is allowed, so eligibility returns without a valid exception. (c) Restore original valid exception and 100000 request but set requested_version to a distinct identifier: reject_requested_use, gateversion_binding. Numerical resemblance is not a substitute for evidence binding to the requested artifact. None of these outputs exercises real approval authority.

  9. Illustrative decision. Refuse unrestricted use of a single asserted three-year value. The current family supports 82–94 under its imposed c restriction and identical calibration; choosing 88 has no data-identification proof. The developer owns a proposal for additional data, an economically justified restriction or a narrower use. An independent challenger reviews that proposal and the affected exposure. Any permitted interim activity should be explicit—for example, scenario analysis reporting the entire range rather than production reliance on one point—and bind the actual version, notional, review date and responsible authority. Expiry or a new quote outside the assumed range triggers reevaluation; closure requires reproducible evidence resolving the requested target or an approved restricted use with documented residual uncertainty. Calling the target identified or empirically validated is not a temporary waiver available to a committee.

    Criteria. Full credit requires scope and decision, the 12 CU quantitative range, accountable ownership and meaningful challenge, a finite expiry/trigger, testable closure evidence, and separation of permissible operational restriction from an unsupported mathematical assertion. Other responses may choose refusal or tightly controlled exploratory use if the consequences and remaining evidence gaps are explicit. A date and signature without these elements are insufficient.

  10. Illustrative referee response. The null coefficient in the curve family produces identical fitted quotes but year-3 prices 82–94; exact fit does not identify the requested value or prove the family true. Independent arithmetic checks can establish conditional implementation behavior, while intended cash rights and empirical outcomes need different evidence. The three-unit comparison passes every 0.02 tolerance but produces signed 4 and gross 6 CU against 3/5 limits; portfolio size and error dependence matter. Disjoint row IDs rule out literal duplicate rows only, not shared information, event dependence or later-outcome leakage. Finally, the size-only exception changes a notional gate; it expressly leaves version and substantive validation gates intact.

    A reproducible packet binds contract, version and inputs; exact benchmark cases and tolerances with units; calibration objective and identification/conditioning analysis; frozen out-of-sample design and data lineage; signed/gross financial consequences; current limitations and findings; named owners/challenge/decision authority; scope, expiry and escalation. Include every failed material check rather than selecting only favorable outputs. The dated primary US guidance supplies context, not Sable's numerical limits, an institution-specific legal conclusion or proof of model adequacy.

    Evaluation. Full credit requires correcting all five claims, at least two correctly explained quantitative examples, an operationally reproducible packet, distinct computational and empirical evidence, and accurate source/threshold scope. Alternative controls are acceptable when they address the actual failure and produce reviewable closure evidence; a generic approval checklist without quantitative consequences is inadequate.

Teach-back and delayed retention

Teach-back. Explain why a model can fit, calculate and pass local tests while still being unsuitable for a requested use. Describe one finding that changes the decision.

Answer standard. Fitting addresses selected calibration observations; correct calculation addresses a specified mathematical target; neither alone identifies an extrapolated payoff or verifies the actual contract and data. Position scale, correlated errors and unsupported use can change the consequence. A useful finding supplies a reproducer, affected scope, quantitative consequence, owner and closure test—for example, a 12 CU curve-family range that blocks a three-year point-valuation request until supported information or a restricted use resolves it.

After 7–14 days, without notes: (i) give the year-3 loading on c in the polynomial family; (ii) compute the year-3 affine quote weights for tenors 1 and 1.5; (iii) bound the error for positions 10 and−20 with simultaneous unit bounds 0.1 and 0.2; (iv) state what a matching file digest proves; (v) explain whether an expired size exception necessarily forbids a smaller request inside the ordinary limit.

Answers. (i)3·2·1=6. (ii)w=4, weights−3,4; the two-quote error amplification factor is 7. (iii)10(0.1)+20(0.2)=5 CU. (iv) It binds a comparison to particular bytes under the chosen digest procedure; it does not prove mathematical or economic correctness. (v) No: the ordinary limit still applies, subject to all other gates. Advancement requires a fresh evidence-to-decision memo in which every material finding has an owner, financial consequence and verifiable disposition.

Sources and the volume synthesis

The SR 26-2 letter and its 17 April 2026 attachment are the dated primary institutional readings. Sable's data, mathematical demonstrations, thresholds, procedures and problems are original. These readings do not establish the synthetic outcomes or certify a particular institution's compliance.

This volume's models produce prices and hedge claims under explicit cash, information and trading assumptions. Governance closes the loop by asking which claims have actually been supported, which numerical and contractual errors remain, and what use the evidence can justify. The Volume 10 assessment and project require an integrated defense across fixed income, derivatives, computation and controlled model use; isolated formula recall is not the completion criterion. Banking and institutional risk in Volume 11 add the balance sheets, liquidity, counterparties and incentives that make these decisions consequential.

Sources and further study

  • Federal Reserve — SR26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April2026) — Dated US institutional context and supersession of SR11-7/SR21-8; not a source of Sable data, thresholds or proof of regulatory compliance.
  • Federal Reserve, FDIC and OCC — Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April2026) — Primary further reading on tailored quantitative-model governance, scope, effective challenge, development/use, validation/monitoring and third parties. Synthetic procedures and mathematical examples are original.
